video_title: Knicks Advance to ECF! Jalen & Josh React to SWEEP 🧹 | Is Philly is a Sports Town?

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Philly is not a sports town if the owner buys tickets

text_blocks.speaker: Josh Hart
text_blocks.text: You can't have your guy like I'm sit there say, oh yeah, obviously we love our fans, we all need them to come to support. But come on now. The owner can't be out here buying thousands of tickets so Knicks fans don't get their hands on them. That's not

text_blocks.speaker: Jalen Brunson
text_blocks.text: I get it. I get it. I just when you say Minneapolis is more of a sports town than Philly, that's where I got to draw the line.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart complains about the long break between playoff series
quotes.quote: A sweep is great, right? You know what I mean? But dog, seven days, minimum, off? No games? That's torture. Like torture. I'm over here doing nothing. Hanging up art. Just to feel something. Adam. Come on, we got to lock in.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' 'punch first' mentality creates doubt in opponents during playoffs
quotes.quote: It's always tough in those close out games. Your goal always is to come out aggressive the beginning of the game, that first quarter, especially that first half. And then you want doubt to kind of seep into the opponent. Like we're up 3-0 in the series and we're up 12 points in this game right now, this close out game. And then you want that that doubt to start seeping in of like, okay, I don't know if we can come back from this one or this might be the end for the season. And more that that doubt continues to seep in, it aids in your goal to close it out. And I feel like that's something that we did very well the last two close out games was punched them at the beginning of the game and just keep punching.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Not giving opponents momentum or opportunity is crucial in playoffs
quotes.quote: I'm curious to see tonight of that Cleveland and Detroit series because obviously Cleveland was up. They handled business in that second half. They got up like 15-20 and then the end of the game, at one point it got to like an eight-point game with a minute left in the game. Those guys in Detroit came out and they came off the bench and kept the energy. So it's like you never want to give teams or players or whoever it is in the postseason momentum or opportunity because that could be a difference maker. Sasser played well. What if Detroit is like, you know what? He played well. We need shooting. You throw him in Game 5 and he hits two, three, four threes and that can change the outcome of a game. Not saying that's going to happen tonight, but you don't want any of those opportunities.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart explains his offensive approach and impact on the Knicks
quotes.quote: I'm not going to lie. I thought I would get more just like open clean looks against Philly. And I was excited about that because I was just like, all right, I'll probably have Joel on me or he was hurt, Drummond, or whatever it was and I'll just kind of get those easy looks. That wasn't the case at first. I look at Kelly Oubre and I'm like, bro, why are you guarding me? Go harass somebody else. But I think even when I'm not making shots, I still feel like I have the ability to get in the paint, especially games like that where obviously they play a little bit of slower pace and able to rebound and push it. I'm able to kind of get into the lane and get early shots and quick shots and kind of negate that to a certain extent. But I do think we're doing a better job of, you know, if teams are playing off me, I know how to use that to my advantage in terms of whether I'm if I'm shooting the ball well with confidence, cool. If not, I'm able to get into pick and rolls, DHOs, stuff like that. And I'm making that that big still have to work. So now instead of me getting an open shot, it's figure out a way of how can I get JB open off the screen because I know if I screen his man, if my guy's all the way in the paint, it's going to be tough for him because he's going to have to either get back up and stop the JB's pocket three or sit back and rock with that. Or now JB gets to dictate what he wants, especially with Kelly Oubre with some of those rifle actions, allowing him to get downhill.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart praises Miles McBride's defensive intensity and consistency
quotes.quote: He takes those things personal. When he has a match up or especially if someone says something, he gets he gets in those modes and he's just like, bro, I'm just I'm I'm guarding this person no matter what. Don't switch me off him. And I'm going to I'm going to I'm going to lock him up. So his his defense should definitely get some some credit and some love because especially guarding Maxey who's it's that was a good that's a good power move right there. Not even his defense, but I feel like everything since was it Game 6? What was what was the the point where we were like that was the turning point for him in the Hawks series? I forget. The Hawks series he played played well defensively the whole time. I think offensively the first couple games, I don't think he shot the ball that well, but if you look at his defense, it's been top tier all playoffs. And fortunately, we're in a position where it's like we can get away with if Kelly Oubre doesn't shoot the ball that well in a game, we're not relying on it. We have other guys. We have JB, Cat, Deuce come in, OG. So that's like also the the benefit of having the talent that we have is not so much pressure on one person. What we talked about with JB earlier. He doesn't have to feel the need to go out there and score 35 for us to be in the game. He can sit there and score 20 and have eight assists and we're in the game at the end where we want to be. So, he's been hooping.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart avoids outside noise to maintain focus during the season
quotes.quote: During this process we always we always talk about it, right? We want the fans, the supporters and all that to have as much fun as they can. We want them to enjoy these moments and these games and series and stuff like that. But for us it's like we don't we don't really want to think about it. Maybe in the summer, when we're removed from actual games and that kind of thing and you can kind of take a step back and like talk to a fan or whatever like that and you see the impact they have, like that's cool. But while you're in it, you really don't think about it. You don't really want don't really even want to hear it because because once once you start doing that, you start opening the door to the outside noise. And now you're you're kind of locked in on the task at hand of the Eastern Conference Finals, but you're also subconsciously listening to these people telling you you're great or what these people say on a sports show or whatever it is. So now you're not fully 100% locked in. You might be 80 and 20, but sometimes that 20 could be the what could win or lose you a game in terms of focus and those kind of things. So while we're in the midst of it, we don't really want to hear it, we don't really want to think about it because we have a goal and we haven't got to that goal yet. But down the road in the summer or something, we kick back and chill and drink some wine and talk, you know, maybe we enjoy those moments then.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart believes the Premier League title race is rigged by VAR
quotes.quote: The Premier League title race has been rigged. VAR is probably the worst, most biased, controversial thing that there is in sports. Arsenal, the fact that they have no penalties given away, no red cards with countless of ones that should have been penalties. This season has been kind of absurd. So it was written by the Prem and VAR that they would win this year, so it kind of is what it is. They're going to get slapped by PSG in the Champions League, so that will kind of be a that would be nice. But, this is the most rigged Premier League title race that we've seen in recent years.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart has lost faith in Chelsea due to poor management and performance
quotes.quote: I've come to terms with it. The only thing that can go right for the rest of this race for the Prem is Arsenal bottle it, Tottenham get relegated, and like we're just somewhere in 10th. And like maybe like win the next two games. Like that would be nice. Like that that would be at this point, that would be a win for me. But my club is just not what they were several years ago. Hopefully this summer, we get a little more, you know, experience, some good vets, some people that can, you know, create big chances, put the ball in the back of the net, stop them from getting the ball in the back of the net because we haven't got a clean sheet since N'Golo Kanté. It would be nice. So, no, I don't have faith. I would love my club to win. I don't have faith.
